sentences.text:
Dr.G.Srinivas vs Sriram General Insuranse Company ... on 11
September, 2024

Author: P.Sam Koshy
Bench: P.Sam Koshy, N.Tukaramji
 The Honourable Sri Justice P.Sam Koshy
 And
 The Honourable Sri Justice N.Tukaramji
 I.A.No.1 Of 2024 In/And C.M.A No.459 of 2024
Common Judgment

:
(per Hon'ble Sri Justice P.Sam Koshy) The present is an appeal which has been filed assailing the order dated 15.09.2022 passed by the I-Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court at Secunderabad in I.A.No.1775 of 2016 in M.V.O.P.No.338 of 2013.
2.

entities.text: I-Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court at Secunderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Vide the impugned order, the Court below has dismissed the application filed by the appellant under Order IX Rule 9 read with Section 151 of the CPC seeking for setting aside of the dismissal of M.V.O.P.No.338 of 2013 dated 20.09.2016.
The appellant herein, the claimant before the trial Court, had filed a motor vehicle claim case for certain grievous injuries suffered by him from an accident that took place on 01.06.2010.
The said petition was registered as M.V.O.P.No.338 of 2013.
Notices were issued.
The respondents proceeded ex parte in the original claim case and the matter was fixed for the evidence.
The chief affidavit was also filed.

However, on the fateful day i.e.,
20.09.2016 for certain unavoidable reasons, the claimant as also the counsel could not appear before the trial Court and the matter stood dismissed for default on 20.09.2016.
3. Not less than a month's time on 17.10.2016 itself, the application under Order IX Rule 9 read with 151 of the CPC was filed seeking for restoration of the claim petition.
It was this petition which was registered as I.A.No.1775 of 2016.

The restoration petition was dragged on before the trial Court for a period of six years before the impugned order was passed on 15.09.2022 and after a lapse of six years, the trial Court dismissed the restoration petition.
The present appeal under Order XLIII Rule 1 of the CPC is one challenging the said order dated 15.09.2022.
There is a delay of 628 days in filing the present appeal.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that there was communication gap between the counsel who had appeared before the trial Court in the restoration petition and finally when the claimant came to know about it immediately he filed the same and has also prayed for sympathetic consideration of I.A.No.1 of 2024 which is petition for condonation of delay of 628 days in filing the present appeal.
5. Admittedly, the claim petition under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is a welfare legislation enacted for the welfare of the people who meet with motor accidents.

Therefore, in the Dr.G.Srinivas vs Sriram General Insuranse Company ... on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154800258/
1 opinion of this Bench the matter was one which the trial Court ought to have considered more pragmatically by taking a more liberal view rather than going on the technicalities and by applying the law regarding restoration of the claim petition strictly.

entities.text: Dr.G.Srinivas vs Sriram General Insuranse Company
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Court should have also considered the fact that it is a welfare legislation and it was the claimant who had defaulted in his appearance and the respondents had already stood ex parte before the trial Court, as such, the respondents would not be put to any prejudice.

The trial Court could have restored the petition on some conditions like restricting the claim of interest for the period the petitioner had defaulted rather than dismissing the entire claim petition itself and also subsequently dismissing the restoration petition also.

6. The Supreme Court in a series of decisions has repeatedly held that when restoration petitions that are filed, particularly arising out of welfare legislation, the applications are required to be considered sympathetically, more pragmatically and taking a liberal view.
7.
Today, the matter is taken up for admission and on condonation of delay, what strikes the conscience of this Court is that the claim petition was one for grievous injuries suffered by the appellant.
The claim petition was one that was filed way back in the year 2013 which itself by now is 11 years old.
If we issue notice to the respondents on this appeal, on the restoration petition that has been rejected by the trial Court, this may further consume time to the detriment of the claimants.

8. Therefore, to meet the ends of justice, we are of the considered opinion that it would be more appropriate if we allow the present appeal by setting aside the rejection of the restoration petition and allowing I.A.No.1775 of 2016 and remit the matter back to the trial Court for proceeding with M.V.O.P.No.338 of 2013 from the stage the matter stood on the date of dismissal of the claim petition i.e., 20.09.2016.
The learned Court is further directed to proceed further and decide the claim petition on priority basis at the earliest.

9. However, considering the fact that since there appears to be a definite lapse on the part of the claimant in not pursuing his claim diligently during the intervening period, we are of the considered view that let the interest payable to the claimant on the compensation whatsoever that shall be quantified be paid to him from the date of allowing the present civil miscellaneous appeal today i.e.,
from 11.09.2024.
10. I.A.No.1 of 2024 and the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal stands allowed and disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.

____________________ P.SAM KOSHY, J ____________________ N. TUKARAMJI, J 11.09.2024 Pl/Lrkm Dr.G.Srinivas vs Sriram General Insuranse Company ... on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154800258/
